mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drags down S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.7%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent increase in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above their 6-month moving averages signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate above 5% for four consecutive months, combined with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS), signals deepening labor market distress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% for 4 consecutive months AND PAYEMS falls for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.8%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation exists between the housing starts index (HOUST) and S&P 500 forward returns at the 5-day horizon, as new housing construction signals broader economic activity and confidence, which supports corporate earnings and equity valuations.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST changes and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) over any 3-year rolling window.
